messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: [Name]

Sex: Male

Age: 76 years

Medical Record No.: [Number]

Hospital Admission Date: [Date]

Discharge Date: [Date]

Hospital Course:

A 76-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with an incidental 4 cm left renal mass, which was treated with a left partial nephrectomy. Upon pathological examination, it was discovered that the patient was suffering from WHO/ISUP grade 1, TNM stage pT1 clear cell RCC, with the resection margin positive for the tumor.

The patient underwent a right radical orchiectomy when he was found to have a metastatic tumor in the right testis. The metastatic tumor was two centimeters in size, and it was confined to the testicular parenchyma.

Fourteen months after the orchiectomy, he underwent a completion left radical nephrectomy due to the recurrence of the tumor.

Ongoing imaging surveillance discovered several soft tissue masses in the left posterior chest wall, as well as masses in the pancreas. A two-centimeter enhancing mass was found in the upper pole of the right kidney 87 months following the orchiectomy.

The patient has been offered systemic therapy of VEGF inhibitor and discharged with continued medical supervision. He is alive with disease, 93 months post-orchiectomy.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Status:

The patient is discharged with continued medical supervision.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
**C64**

The admission was for a left renal mass treated by partial nephrectomy, with pathology confirming clear cell renal cell carcinoma. That makes the primary malignancy of the kidney (C64) the principal diagnosis for this episode.

This is a judgement call because the summary compresses roughly 8 years of disease into one narrative. If the episode being coded were actually the later presentation, the answer could change:
- **C79 (secondary malignancy):** if the admission was treatment aimed at the metastases, such as the testicular, chest wall or pancreatic deposits, as in Example 6.
- **C64 still:** if the right kidney mass were treated as a new primary.

Because the diagnosis section is withheld and the summary states the admission was for the left renal mass, C64 is the most defensible code.
